_metadata.description: The operator console and the obligations that only appear once there are users.

requirements.title: Console covers every perceivable state
requirements.description: Graph view, offer detail and promotion actions each render loading, empty, partial, stale and error states. Status is never colour-only: every status chip carries a text label and the graph view has a table equivalent.

validation.notes: Feature tests assert each state renders with its documented selector.
BAS case walks the console and asserts the accessible names of status controls.

requirements.title: Promotion is an explicit operator action
requirements.description: The console's promotion control states what will change before it is used and shows the proposing actor and rationale where a proposal exists.

validation.notes: The control is absent or disabled for a non-operator role.

requirements.title: Per-offer compliance obligations carry review dates
requirements.description: Offers carry the legal and platform obligations they incur — disclosure requirements, marketplace terms, tax treatment — each with a review date. The source catalog records these as prose per revenue line, where nothing surfaces them before a launch.

validation.notes: An obligation past its review date surfaces on the offer and on the board.

requirements.title: Offer books are scoped independently
requirements.description: More than one offer graph can exist in one instance, each queried independently. This is what makes the scenario usable by an operator whose business is not this one.

validation.notes: A query scoped to one book never returns nodes from another.

requirements.title: Triggers can read another scenario's live state
requirements.description: A trigger clause may name a fact served by another scenario rather than one an operator supplied, so a condition like 'the dependency scenario is deployable' evaluates itself. Deferred to P2 deliberately: it needs the fact-source contract to be stable, and an unavailable source must evaluate to unknown rather than false, which the P0 evaluation rule already establishes.

validation.notes: A scenario-sourced fact resolves through a faked client; an unavailable source yields unknown, never false.
Evaluation over a mixed operator/scenario fact set records the source of each fact consulted.
